tools.name: create_project
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Creates the necessary directory structure and configuration files to begin scanning a codebase with Coverity.

PREREQUISITES: None - this tool MUST be called first before any other tools for a project.

WHEN TO USE:
- First-time setup for a new project
- Changing Coverity installation directory/version
- User requests "create project", "setup Coverity", "initialize project"

WORKFLOW GUIDANCE:
INTERACTIVE SETUP - When users haven't provided all parameters, guide them through:
1. COVERITY INSTALLATION LOCATION:
   Question: "Where is your Coverity installation located?"
   Options:
   - "Provide installation directory path" (user specifies path like /opt/coverity/2024.12)
   - "Use system PATH" (coverity_install_dir = "")
   - "Help me find it" (provide guidance on locating Coverity)

2. COVERITY CONNECT INTEGRATION (optional):
   Question: "Do you want to use Coverity Connect integration to speed up incremental scans?"
   Options:
   - "Yes, configure Connect integration" (ask follow-up for URL and stream)
   - "No, skip Connect integration" (don't set stream/connect_url)

   If YES, ask follow-up questions:
   - "What is your Coverity Connect server URL?" (e.g., https://connect.company.com)
   - "What is the stream name in Connect?" (e.g., my-project-stream)

3. BUILD COMMANDS (optional):
   Question: "Do you use specific clean and build commands for your project?"
   Options:
   - "Yes, I have custom build commands" (ask for clean_command and build_command)
   - "I don't know - please detect and suggest commands" (analyze project files to determine build system)
   - "No, skip build configuration" (don't set build commands)

   If "Yes", ask follow-up questions:
   - "What command cleans your project?" (e.g., make clean, gradle clean)
   - "What command builds your project?" (e.g., make, gradle build)

   If "I don't know", LLM should:
   1. Use Glob tool to look for build system indicators.  Examples:
      - "Makefile" → suggest "make clean" and "make"
      - "pom.xml" → suggest "mvn clean" and "mvn compile"
      - "build.gradle*" → suggest "gradle clean" and "gradle build"
      - "package.json" → check scripts, suggest "npm run clean" and "npm run build"
      - "CMakeLists.txt" → suggest "make clean" and "make" (or cmake equivalent)
      - "*.sln" or "*.csproj" → suggest "dotnet clean" and "dotnet build"
   2. Present findings and ask for confirmation before proceeding
   3. If multiple build systems detected, ask user to choose
   4. If no build system detected, explain and offer to skip or let user specify manually

DIRECT USAGE - Skip interactive setup when:
- All required parameters provided
- User explicitly requests non-interactive setup

ERROR HANDLING: If project exists and force=false, returns clear error with current Coverity version and guidance to use force=true for version changes.

NEXT STEPS: After setup, use run_scan to perform the actual analysis.

build_command.description: Build command to use during scan; must be specified if clean_command is specified

clean_command.description: Clean command to run before building; must be specified if build_command is specified

connect_url.description: URL of the Coverity Connect server to use to get scan summary information to speed up HFI scans; must be specified if stream is specified

coverity_install_dir.description: Path to the Coverity installation directory (containing bin/coverity). Use empty string "" to search on system PATH.

force.description: Force recreation of existing project setup (allows changing Coverity installation directory/version)

project_dir.description: Path to the project directory to analyze

stream_name.description: Name of a Coverity Connect stream to use to get scan summary information to speed up HFI scans; must be specified if connect_url is specified

tools.name: run_scan
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Perform static analysis scanning of source code using Coverity to identify quality issues, and security vulnerabilities.

PREREQUISITES: create_project must be completed first.

CRITICAL: All first-time scans and PFI incremental scans MUST use task-augmented execution. HFI incremental scans can be executed without task augmentation.

WHEN TO USE:
- User requests code scanning or analysis
- After significant code changes
- Before merging to main branch (PFI mode)
- Quick pre-commit checks (HFI mode)

SUPPORTED LANGUAGES:
Coverity has support for scanning the following languages:

With Build Capture (requires a build command to capture compilation):
- C/C++
- Objective-C/C++ (not suppported on Linux ARM64)
- Java
- C# (Supported on Linux AMD64 and Windows AMD64 only)
- Visual Basic (Supported on Linux AMD64 and Windows AMD64 only)
- Go
- Kotlin (not supported on Linux ARM64)

Without Build Capture:
- Apex
- JavaScript/TypeScript
- Dart
- Python
- PHP
- Ruby
- Swift
- Configuration (Infra-as-code, e.g. Terraform, CloudFormation)

The following languages can be scanned without build capture, but will have more
accurate results if a build command is provided to capture the compilation:
- Java
- C#
- Go

WORKFLOW GUIDANCE:
SCAN WORKFLOW - When users request a scan:
1. ATTEMPT SCAN FIRST: Try running the scan directly with run_scan
2. HANDLE MISSING PROJECT: If scan fails with "No Coverity project found" error:
   - Inform user that project setup is required first
   - Use create_project interactive setup (ask installation location, Connect settings, build commands)
   - After successful project setup, retry runnning the scan
3. PROCEED WITH SCAN: Continue with scan analysis and report results

EXAMPLE FLOW:
User: "Run a Coverity scan on my project"
LLM: [Calls run_scan] → Gets "No project found" error
LLM: "I need to set up Coverity for your project first. Let me ask a few questions..."
LLM: [Runs interactive create_project setup]
LLM: "Project setup complete! Now running the scan..."
LLM: [Retries run_scan] → Success

HFI SCAN WORKFLOW - For fast incremental scans:
1. Use git status/diff to detect changed files
2. Pass detected files to files_to_scan parameter
3. If no changes: offer PFI scan or manual file specification

PERFORMANCE NOTES:
- CRITICAL: Use task-augmented execution for ALL PFI scans and first-time scans
- HFI scans: Fast, no task augmentation needed

NEXT STEPS: Get issue details for a specific issue using the get_issue_details tool.

build_command.description: Custom build command for this scan - use when incremental scans need to force recompilation of changed files (e.g., 'make modified_file.o'); if not specified, uses the command in the configuration file

files_to_scan.description: Optional list of specific files to scan (paths relative to project directory)

scan_mode.description: Scanning mode for incremental scans: 'pfi' (perfect fidelity incremental - REQUIRES task augmentation) or 'hfi' (high fidelity incremental - fast, no task augmentation needed)

scan_type.description: Type of scan to perform: 'full' (REQUIRES task augmentation), 'incremental' (task augmentation required for PFI mode), 'auto' (REQUIRES task augmentation)

tools.name: get_issues
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Retrieves scan results with issue previews, categorization, and intelligent filtering.

PREREQUISITES: create_project and at least one completed run_scan.

WHEN TO USE:
- Review specific types of issues (security, quality, performance)
- Get issues in recently modified files
- Filter and analyze scan results

WORKFLOW GUIDANCE:
FIX/VERIFY WORKFLOW:
1. VERIFYING FIXES: Use HFI results only to confirm fixes in scanned files
2. FINDING NEW ISSUES: Use PFI results for comprehensive issue analysis
   - Priority: Most recent PFI incremental → Most recent PFI full scan

EXAMPLES:
- High-priority security issues: severities=["High"], kinds=["SECURITY"]
- Issues in recent changes: only_modified=true, prioritize_new=true
- Specific file analysis: file_patterns=["src/auth/**/*.go"]
- Quick overview: limit=5, group_by_file=true

NEXT STEPS: Get detailed information for a specific issue with get_issue_details or review scan history with list_scans.

categories.description: Filter by issue categories; does case insensitive substring matching on issue category field (e.g., ["Error handling issues", "Memory - illegal accesses", "API usage errors"])

cwe_categories.description: Filter by CWE categories but without the CWE prefix (e.g., ["79", "89"])

group_by_file.description: Group issues by file in response for targeted fixing (default: false)

include_preview.description: Whether to include issue previews in response (default: true for LLM-friendly results)

include_summary.description: Include summary statistics in response (default: true for LLM analysis)

limit.description: Maximum number of issues to return in preview (default: 5, prevents overwhelming responses)

offset.description: Number of issues to skip for pagination (default: 0)

only_modified.description: Show only issues in git-modified files for development workflow (default: false)

prioritize_new.description: Prioritize issues in recently modified files in results (default: false)

project_dir.description: Project directory to get the issues for

scope.description: Filter by scan scope (all files or limited file set)

tools.name: get_issue_details
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Retrieves comprehensive details for a specific Coverity issue including execution path and full diagnostic information.

PREREQUISITES: create_project and completed run_scan with the target issue.

WHEN TO USE:
- Get comprehensive details for a specific issue
- Understand execution path and events leading to issue
- Get detailed diagnostic information for fixing

NEXT STEPS: Review the issue details and take appropriate action based on the findings.

merge_key.description: Unique identifier for the issue (typically obtained from get_issues results)

project_dir.description: Project directory to get the issue details for

scope.description: Filter by scan scope (all files or limited file set)

tools.name: list_scans
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Displays history of all Coverity scans performed on a project for tracking analysis history.

PREREQUISITES: create_project must be completed first.

WHEN TO USE:
- Check if project has been scanned before
- Review scan types and timing history
- Decide which scan results to retrieve with get_issues

NOTE: Scans are retrieved in reverse chronological order (newest to oldest).

NEXT STEPS: Use get_issues to get issues for the most recent scan for a given scan type and mode.

limit.description: Maximum number of scans to return (default: 10, max: 50)

offset.description: Number of scans to skip for pagination (default: 0)
